title: Nine-month-olds often sweep food closer with the fingers together
summary: The CDC nine-month movement checklist includes raking food toward the body with the fingers.
body: Around nine months, the CDC Learn the Signs movement list includes a feeding motion it calls raking: the baby uses the fingers to pull food toward himself. The fingers work together as a sweeper, drawing the food in until it is close enough to mouth. That is a different motion from a later thumb-to-finger pinch. CDC puts a skill on these age pages when at least three quarters of children can do it by the birthday printed there. The birth-defects center that issues the pages says they are not a formal screening instrument, so a baby who still misses this sweep is not given a diagnosis by the checklist.
